headline: Meta launches Threads VR app for Meta Quest headsets
summary: Meta's social platform expands to virtual reality, allowing users to browse feeds, post, and watch videos within VR environments.
details: Meta has officially launched a Threads app designed for its Meta Quest virtual reality headsets. This move brings the social media platform into the immersive VR space, following its recent expansion to Ray-Ban smart glasses.

The new Threads VR app offers a comprehensive experience, enabling users to browse their feeds, create posts, like and reply to content, visit profiles, search for users and topics, and watch videos directly within the VR environment.

Meta aims to enhance the social aspect of VR with this dedicated app. The company stated that Threads can enrich the VR experience by allowing users to keep up with conversations during games, discuss shows or music with friends, or simply perform quick check-ins between daily tasks.

headline_marked: [[OpenAI COO Brad Lightcap]] Departs to 'Start Something New'
headline: OpenAI COO Brad Lightcap Departs to 'Start Something New'
summary: After an eight-year tenure, OpenAI's special projects lead and former COO, Brad Lightcap, announced his departure, citing a desire to pursue new ventures.
details: Brad Lightcap, who served as OpenAI's COO and most recently led special projects, has announced his departure from the AI lab after eight years. He revealed his decision in an internal memo, stating his intention to "start something new" and "help you all advance the mission from a different vantage point."

Lightcap's role at OpenAI evolved significantly. He expanded his COO responsibilities in March 2025 to include global deployment and business strategy. By January 2026, he stepped back from product and engineering leadership but retained oversight of commercial functions. In April, he transitioned to a special projects role reporting directly to CEO Sam Altman.

His departure follows a series of high-profile exits from OpenAI's executive team. This includes AGI chief Fidji Simo and CMO Kate Rouch, both of whom left for health reasons. The company has also undergone significant reorganization, with Greg Brockman taking charge of product development as OpenAI prepares for a potential public offering.
